brief: A drone workbench station: a flat covered working top with a bin beside it for screws. Dress it for a build session: a 5 inch quad on the top, a hex driver set and a LiPo battery nearby.

requirements.evidence: Full hex base piece at 0,0,0 with a full top cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top); open faces capped and joints locked.

requirements.requirement: A bin beside the top for screws
requirements.evidence: Second full base piece at 1,0,0 (east neighbour) holding a full-depth hex bin (bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full) filled with an M3 screws bin prop (prop:1).

requirements.requirement: A 5 inch quad on the top
requirements.evidence: quad-5in (prop:5) rests on the top cover, offset west so it clears the screw bin wall; it overhangs the 166x144 mm cover as the surface allows.
hexdriver-set (prop:4) stands on the bench about two cells west of the station, clear of the quad.
lipo-4s (prop:6) lies on the bench beside the hex driver set.

finish.summary: Built a drone workbench: a full hex base with a covered top, a neighbouring base holding a full-depth screws bin, and capped/locked joints. The 5 in quad sits on the top cover, the hex driver set and a 4S LiPo are on the bench nearby. The hex driver set and LiPo could not share the cover with the 281 mm quad, so they sit on the bench. The screws prop sits below the bin rim (a PROP_BELOW_RIM hint, but check_build reports no prop warnings). meshClash is clear and there are no rule issues. Materials and print durability were not assessed.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
